cases.markdown:
## Production purchases and variety assumptions

Research checked 11 October 2026. Buy only proposed stock after checking local suitability. Existing plants and structures are inventory, not repeat purchases. Early/middle/late describes picking order; compatible flowering is a separate pollination check. Expected seasons describe established production, not guaranteed food this year.

### Feijoa

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: fruit.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Cultivar-dependent pollen compatibility: Primary Brazilian germplasm experiment found both compatibility classes. Biological evidence supports checking the actual cultivar and compatible pollen, not assigning one universal species category or copying its calendar to South Africa.

South African research context: Government confirms ARC evaluated feijoa; no trial result, cultivar, harvest month or yield follows from this mention.

Check the actual cultivar's pollen needs. A primary trial includes self-compatible and self-incompatible plants.

Record local ripe picking dates and output. Foreign cultivar seasons do not establish a South African season.

Buying advice: Ask the nursery to name the cultivar or identify a seedling and provide local fruiting and compatible-pollen evidence. 'Fruit Salad Tree' is a common sales label and does not identify a tested cultivar.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [dos Santos et al. (2007), Evidence of late-acting self-incompatibility in Acca sellowiana, Revista Brasileira de Fruticultura 29(1)](https://new.scielo.br/j/rbf/a/3Wh7WGGbVFkHckM7R5GDJLc/?ilang=pt_BR&lang=pt)

Source: [South African Yearbook 2003/04, ARC tropical/subtropical crop research](https://www.gcis.gov.za/sites/default/files/docs/resourcecentre/yearbook/2004/18scitec.pdf)

### Quiver tree

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: young flower buds.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Young flower-bud food use: The edible product is the young flower bud. June–July flowering does not establish the exact pre-opening picking dates, first bud-bearing age or edible kg/plant.

Match cultivation to this arid-land tree and well-drained conditions.

Record young-bud picking separately from flowering or ornamental growth.

Buying advice: Obtain correctly identified legal nursery stock and local growing advice. No food-yield cultivar or maturity curve is verified.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Aloidendron dichotomum](https://pza.sanbi.org/aloidendron-dichotomum)

### Pineapple

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: Pineapple fruit; whole fruit and processed portions have different weights.

First crop reference: 18 months. Hluhluwe production-cycle reference: 18 months / 12 = 1.5 years. The source explicitly says cycle length varies greatly. Starting material, cultivar, weather and flower initiation matter; this is neither a universal first-harvest date nor a 12-month annual yield. Actual timing depends on variety and site care.

Hluhluwe crop-cycle output: Regional hectare reference: conservative 50 t/ha, average 60–75 t/ha, good 80 t/ha per production crop. The same page describes a normal 18-month Hluhluwe cycle. These are not kg/plant/year or a forecast for a household planting.

Cultivar and renewal choice: Queen and Smooth Cayenne serve different uses. The guide's example fruit weights (Queen 0.75 kg; Smooth Cayenne 2 kg) are cultivar descriptions, not annual yields per plant. Queen is re-established after the plant crop in this system.

Climate and calendar conditions: Frost sensitivity and drainage constrain the site. Year-round planting at Hluhluwe is a planting reference, not an all-year household picking window; cooler sites use warmer planting months.

Use a warm, frost-free, well-drained site. The KZN production reference is Hluhluwe; it does not establish suitability throughout South Africa.

Record planting and actual picking dates. Year-round commercial planting or marketing does not mean every planted pineapple gives fruit in every month.

Buying advice: KZN guide: Queen is a fresh-fruit candidate; Smooth Cayenne is mainly a processing candidate. Confirm clean crowns/suckers, local suitability and crop-cycle advice with a nursery. Queen re-establishment after the plant crop belongs in the future plan.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple: Bearing Age, p. 22](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple, p. 22](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple: Spacing and Cultivars, p. 22](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple: Climate and Planting Times, p. 22](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

### Waterblommetjie

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: flowers and flower buds.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Waterblommetjie food product and establishment: Western Cape pond food; vigorous winter/spring flowering and winter shop availability are qualitative seasonal evidence, not a numeric picking calendar. Seedlings reach flowering size in one season under ideal conditions, not a universal age-in-years guarantee.

Ideal seedling establishment: Qualitative ideal-condition establishment duration; it is not inserted into a generic tree-age curve.

Start tubers in loam in shallow pond water; move deeper into sun after strong growth.

Record edible flowers/buds and pond area. Dormant tubers resume growth as autumn water returns in the winter-rainfall cycle.

Buying advice: Obtain correctly identified pond plants. Confirm local pond conditions and actual picking dates; no pond-area yield or planting density is sourced.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Aponogeton distachyos](https://pza.sanbi.org/aponogeton-distachyos)

### Rooibos

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: young shoots for dried rooibos tea.

First crop reference: 12–18 months. First commercial cutting readiness at 12–18 months in the described Cape production system. The account discusses sowing and transfer to plantations but does not explicitly define whether the clock starts at sowing or planting out. Confirm starting stock and timing locally. This is tea-shoot establishment, not fruit-tree bearing. Actual timing depends on variety and site care.

Commercial tea cutting cycle and product: Selected commercial rooibos forms in the Cederberg winter-rainfall region are cut annually December–April, retaining older branches. Cut shoots are chopped, bruised, oxidised and dried. Fresh shoot kg and dried tea kg are separate products. The account describes replacement after up to five harvest years, not a mature kg/plant curve.

Match planting to acidic, sandy winter-rainfall soils and locally suitable rooibos forms.

Keep fresh-cut shoot weights separate from processed dried tea; record the actual processing output.

Buying advice: Ask a local rooibos nursery or adviser for correctly identified, locally proven planting material. The Cape cycle is not a nationwide tea forecast.

Expected picking season: no single local cultivar window established. Reference seasons below are not a forecast.

Reference only — Cederberg / Western Cape winter-rainfall commercial rooibos: Dec–Apr.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Aspalathus linearis](https://pza.sanbi.org/aspalathus-linearis)

### Creeping foxglove

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: leaves for cooked greens.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Documented leaf food use: The article explicitly identifies the catalogue subspecies and edible leaves. Spring/summer flowering is not a leaf-picking calendar.

Use a moist growing position, with semi-shade or sun where water is adequate.

Control rooted runners so this fast groundcover does not smother neighbouring plants.

Buying advice: Buy correctly identified subspecies material. Record actual leaf-cutting dates and weights; no local yield variety or first-cutting duration is verified.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Asystasia gangetica subsp. micrantha](https://pza.sanbi.org/asystasia-gangetica)

### Powder-puff tree

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: young leaves reported edible — specialist review needed.

Food-use review: confirm identity, edible part and appropriate preparation with a qualified local adviser before including this plant as household food. Held out of ordinary food totals and picking jobs.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Edible-part and safety review: The same source reports poison in seeds, bark, wood and roots. Guava-like fruit appearance is not evidence of edible fruit.

Poisonous parts must remain visible: The account records fish-stunning use. No such use is recommended, and no household fruit food claim is made.

Keep this tree in mapped inventory and do not count it as household food until identity and a safe edible-leaf preparation are reviewed.

SANBI describes humid coastal/estuarine conditions and no tolerance of even mild frost.

Age 3: 10,000 kg/ha; age 6: 20,000 kg/ha; sustainable average about 22,500 kg/ha. Same-study density permits equivalents of 50 kg/tree at age 3 and 100 kg/tree at age 6; there is no reference for every intermediate age. lines: 1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: Pineapple fruit; whole fruit and processed portions have different weights.

First crop reference: 18 months. Hluhluwe production-cycle reference: 18 months / 12 = 1.5 years. The source explicitly says cycle length varies greatly. Hluhluwe crop-cycle output: Regional hectare reference: conservative 50 t/ha, average 60–75 t/ha, good 80 t/ha per production crop. The same page describes a normal 18-month Hluhluwe cycle. These are not kg/plant/year or a forecast for a household planting.

Cultivar and renewal choice: Queen and Smooth Cayenne serve different uses. The guide's example fruit weights (Queen 0.75 kg; Smooth Cayenne 2 kg) are cultivar descriptions, not annual yields per plant. Queen is re-established after the plant crop in this system.

Climate and calendar conditions: Frost sensitivity and drainage constrain the site. Year-round planting at Hluhluwe is a planting reference, not an all-year household picking window; cooler sites use warmer planting months.
Use a warm, frost-free, well-drained site. The KZN production reference is Hluhluwe; it does not establish suitability throughout South Africa.
Record planting and actual picking dates. Year-round commercial planting or marketing does not mean every planted pineapple gives fruit in every month.

Buying advice: KZN guide: Queen is a fresh-fruit candidate; Smooth Cayenne is mainly a processing candidate. Confirm clean crowns/suckers, local suitability and crop-cycle advice with a nursery. Queen re-establishment after the plant crop belongs in the future plan.
Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Expected picking season: no single local cultivar window established. Reference seasons below are not a forecast.

cases.markdown:
## Production purchases and variety assumptions

Research checked 11 October 2026. Buy only proposed stock after checking local suitability. Existing plants and structures are inventory, not repeat purchases. Early/middle/late describes picking order; compatible flowering is a separate pollination check. Expected seasons describe established production, not guaranteed food this year.

### Feijoa

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: fruit.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Cultivar-dependent pollen compatibility: Primary Brazilian germplasm experiment found both compatibility classes. Biological evidence supports checking the actual cultivar and compatible pollen, not assigning one universal species category or copying its calendar to South Africa.

South African research context: Government confirms ARC evaluated feijoa; no trial result, cultivar, harvest month or yield follows from this mention.

Check the actual cultivar's pollen needs. A primary trial includes self-compatible and self-incompatible plants.

Record local ripe picking dates and output. Foreign cultivar seasons do not establish a South African season.

Buying advice: Ask the nursery to name the cultivar or identify a seedling and provide local fruiting and compatible-pollen evidence. 'Fruit Salad Tree' is a common sales label and does not identify a tested cultivar.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [dos Santos et al. (2007), Evidence of late-acting self-incompatibility in Acca sellowiana, Revista Brasileira de Fruticultura 29(1)](https://new.scielo.br/j/rbf/a/3Wh7WGGbVFkHckM7R5GDJLc/?ilang=pt_BR&lang=pt)

Source: [South African Yearbook 2003/04, ARC tropical/subtropical crop research](https://www.gcis.gov.za/sites/default/files/docs/resourcecentre/yearbook/2004/18scitec.pdf)

### Quiver tree

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: young flower buds.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Young flower-bud food use: The edible product is the young flower bud. June–July flowering does not establish the exact pre-opening picking dates, first bud-bearing age or edible kg/plant.

Match cultivation to this arid-land tree and well-drained conditions.

Record young-bud picking separately from flowering or ornamental growth.

Buying advice: Obtain correctly identified legal nursery stock and local growing advice. No food-yield cultivar or maturity curve is verified.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Aloidendron dichotomum](https://pza.sanbi.org/aloidendron-dichotomum)

### Pineapple

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: Pineapple fruit; whole fruit and processed portions have different weights.

First crop reference: 18 months. Hluhluwe production-cycle reference: 18 months / 12 = 1.5 years. The source explicitly says cycle length varies greatly. Starting material, cultivar, weather and flower initiation matter; this is neither a universal first-harvest date nor a 12-month annual yield. Actual timing depends on variety and site care.

Hluhluwe crop-cycle output: Regional hectare reference: conservative 50 t/ha, average 60–75 t/ha, good 80 t/ha per production crop. The same page describes a normal 18-month Hluhluwe cycle. These are not kg/plant/year or a forecast for a household planting.

Cultivar and renewal choice: Queen and Smooth Cayenne serve different uses. The guide's example fruit weights (Queen 0.75 kg; Smooth Cayenne 2 kg) are cultivar descriptions, not annual yields per plant. Queen is re-established after the plant crop in this system.

Climate and calendar conditions: Frost sensitivity and drainage constrain the site. Year-round planting at Hluhluwe is a planting reference, not an all-year household picking window; cooler sites use warmer planting months.

Use a warm, frost-free, well-drained site. The KZN production reference is Hluhluwe; it does not establish suitability throughout South Africa.

Record planting and actual picking dates. Year-round commercial planting or marketing does not mean every planted pineapple gives fruit in every month.

Buying advice: KZN guide: Queen is a fresh-fruit candidate; Smooth Cayenne is mainly a processing candidate. Confirm clean crowns/suckers, local suitability and crop-cycle advice with a nursery. Queen re-establishment after the plant crop belongs in the future plan.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple: Bearing Age, p. 22](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple, p. 22](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple: Spacing and Cultivars, p. 22](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple: Climate and Planting Times, p. 22](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

### Waterblommetjie

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: flowers and flower buds.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Waterblommetjie food product and establishment: Western Cape pond food; vigorous winter/spring flowering and winter shop availability are qualitative seasonal evidence, not a numeric picking calendar. Seedlings reach flowering size in one season under ideal conditions, not a universal age-in-years guarantee.

Ideal seedling establishment: Qualitative ideal-condition establishment duration; it is not inserted into a generic tree-age curve.

Start tubers in loam in shallow pond water; move deeper into sun after strong growth.

Record edible flowers/buds and pond area. Dormant tubers resume growth as autumn water returns in the winter-rainfall cycle.

Buying advice: Obtain correctly identified pond plants. Confirm local pond conditions and actual picking dates; no pond-area yield or planting density is sourced.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Aponogeton distachyos](https://pza.sanbi.org/aponogeton-distachyos)

### Rooibos

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: young shoots for dried rooibos tea.

First crop reference: 12–18 months. First commercial cutting readiness at 12–18 months in the described Cape production system. The account discusses sowing and transfer to plantations but does not explicitly define whether the clock starts at sowing or planting out. Confirm starting stock and timing locally. This is tea-shoot establishment, not fruit-tree bearing. Actual timing depends on variety and site care.

Commercial tea cutting cycle and product: Selected commercial rooibos forms in the Cederberg winter-rainfall region are cut annually December–April, retaining older branches. Cut shoots are chopped, bruised, oxidised and dried. Fresh shoot kg and dried tea kg are separate products. The account describes replacement after up to five harvest years, not a mature kg/plant curve.

Match planting to acidic, sandy winter-rainfall soils and locally suitable rooibos forms.

Keep fresh-cut shoot weights separate from processed dried tea; record the actual processing output.

Buying advice: Ask a local rooibos nursery or adviser for correctly identified, locally proven planting material. The Cape cycle is not a nationwide tea forecast.

Expected picking season: no single local cultivar window established. Reference seasons below are not a forecast.

Reference only — Cederberg / Western Cape winter-rainfall commercial rooibos: Dec–Apr.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Aspalathus linearis](https://pza.sanbi.org/aspalathus-linearis)

### Creeping foxglove

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: leaves for cooked greens.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Documented leaf food use: The article explicitly identifies the catalogue subspecies and edible leaves. Spring/summer flowering is not a leaf-picking calendar.

Use a moist growing position, with semi-shade or sun where water is adequate.

Control rooted runners so this fast groundcover does not smother neighbouring plants.

Buying advice: Buy correctly identified subspecies material. Record actual leaf-cutting dates and weights; no local yield variety or first-cutting duration is verified.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Asystasia gangetica subsp. micrantha](https://pza.sanbi.org/asystasia-gangetica)

### Powder-puff tree

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: young leaves reported edible — specialist review needed.

Food-use review: confirm identity, edible part and appropriate preparation with a qualified local adviser before including this plant as household food. Held out of ordinary food totals and picking jobs.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Edible-part and safety review: The same source reports poison in seeds, bark, wood and roots. Guava-like fruit appearance is not evidence of edible fruit.

Poisonous parts must remain visible: The account records fish-stunning use. No such use is recommended, and no household fruit food claim is made.

Keep this tree in mapped inventory and do not count it as household food until identity and a safe edible-leaf preparation are reviewed.

SANBI describes humid coastal/estuarine conditions and no tolerance of even mild frost.

Buying advice: Ask a specialist nursery about lawful provenance and local site fit. Resolve the food-use question before purchasing it as a household crop.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica, barringtonia-racemosa](https://pza.sanbi.org/barringtonia-racemosa)

### Malabar spinach

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: leaves and tender stems.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Leaf vegetable identity and warm-climate culture: Florida extension confirms Malabar spinach as a warm-climate leaf vegetable. Its Florida planting and harvest calendar is not a South African calendar.

Cultivation context: Foreign extension reference for support, seed/cutting propagation and warm, moist conditions; no Florida months are imported into the South African plan.

Optimal from-seed cutting-cycle reference — Florida extension: The extension guide reports maturity around 70 days from seed under optimal conditions, followed by hand trimming leaves and young stems. This foreign optimal-condition duration is supplementary; no South African planting date, exact month window or generic tree-age value is inferred.

Provide climbing support and adequate moisture in a warm growing position.

Record successive leaf harvests by planting batch rather than using tree-age production.

Buying advice: Obtain labelled Basella alba material. A South African regional cultivar, kg/plant benchmark and dated picking window remain unverified.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [UF/IFAS Gardening Solutions: Tropical Spinaches](https://gardeningsolutions.ifas.ufl.edu/plants/edibles/vegetables/tropical-spinaches/)

Source: [UF/IFAS: Cultivation of Malabar Spinach in Florida](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/HS1371)

Source: [UF/IFAS: Florida Cultivation Guide for Malabar Spinach, Harvest and Storage](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/HS1371)

### Brown ivory

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: ripe fruit.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Edible part and local use: January–July is fruit appearance in SANBI's account, not an explicit ripe-picking interval.

Fruit-development duration has context: This is flower-to-fruit development, not years from planting. Its South African January–July fruiting statement is not an observed household picking window.

Use frost-free conditions: SANBI describes frost sensitivity despite drought resistance, with natural low-altitude riverbank bushveld in northern KwaZulu-Natal, Mpumalanga and Limpopo.

Buying advice: Ask for Berchemia discolor, not red ivory (B. zeyheri). Record actual local ripe-picking months.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica, berchemia-discolor](https://pza.sanbi.org/berchemia-discolor)

Source: [World Agroforestry, Agroforestree Database, Berchemia discolor, p. 1](https://apps.worldagroforestry.org/treedb/AFTPDFS/Berchemia_discolor.pdf)

### Shepherd's tree

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: fruit; traditionally prepared flower buds.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Edible part and local use: SANBI also records flower-bud pickle use. Root porridge/coffee references are not instructions to harvest roots or a complete preparation guide.

This hardy, drought-resistant tree occurs in drier southern African regions.

SANBI reports that leaf browsing can taint cattle milk. No feed ration is recommended.

Buying advice: Ask for correctly identified, lawfully sourced stock and check current protected-tree collection requirements before harvesting existing wild trees.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica, boscia-albitrunca](https://pza.sanbi.org/boscia-albitrunca)

### Pigeon pea

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: dry grain or green immature seed; fodder is a separate product.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

SA cultivar maturity and grain trial: Malekutu, Mpumalanga, 1998/99; rainfed mid-December sowing, sandy loam, no fertiliser. Paired days after planting / grain kg/ha: ICPL 88039 127 / 1823; ICPL 85010 129 / 1525; ICPL 87091 140 / 1299; ICPL 87051 193 / 978; ICEAP 00053 231 / 918. Grain differences within each trial were not significant. Visually checked Tables 1–2 (PDF pp43–44). These are dry-grain observations, not green-seed picking dates or nationwide yield defaults.

Tentative newer ARC planting comparison: Potchefstroom 2020/21, good rainfall season: ICEAP01258 versus ICEAP01284 and 22 October versus 25 November sowing. ARC tentatively favours ICEAP01284 in late October and calls for further agro-ecological trials. Exact yield values were not taken from graph bars. Confirm current seed availability; this is not a national cultivar recommendation.

Green seed is timed from flowering: The interval starts at flowering, not sowing. Dry-grain harvest is a separate pod-maturity stage. The broad marketing period does not mean that one planting supplies food continuously.

Record green immature seed and dry grain separately; fodder biomass cannot be counted as household food kg.

Match the selected duration type and sowing date to local frost, rainfall and water availability; the trials retain their own conditions.

Buying advice: Discuss the named SA trial cultivars with a local seed supplier or extension adviser. Current purchase availability and suitability for this site are unverified; do not substitute a cultivar silently.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [Mathews, Silim and Saxena: ICPN 8 (2001), Tables 1–2, printed pp37–38, p. 37](https://oar.icrisat.org/335/1/CO_0013.pdf)

Source: [Bello, Mofokeng and du Toit: SA Graan/Grain, October 2021, pp56–57, p. 57](https://www.arc.agric.za/arc-gci/News%20Articles%20Library/Indigenous%20crops%20can%20help%20with%20food%20security.pdf)

Source: [DAFF: Legume poster, pigeon-pea column, Harvesting row](https://www.nda.gov.za/phocadownloadpap/Brochures_and_Production_Guidelines/Legume%20poster.pdf)

### Pawpaw

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: fruit.

First crop reference: 18 months. KZN typical first crop after planting, about 18 months. The same paragraph reports 9–11 months under favourable Makhathini Flats conditions. This is a typical regional reference, not a minimum or guarantee. Actual timing depends on variety and site care.

Plantation renewal: The KZN guide gives about 4–5 years as the economic life of a plantation. Review replanting in the future plan; this commercial renewal reference does not mean every household plant dies at five or starts full production then.

Regional hectare output: Regional production reference: conservative 10–15 t/ha, average 20–25 t/ha, good 30 t/ha. These area figures are not a per-plant annual age schedule. Match plant sex, bearing plants, spacing, climate and water before setting expected kilograms.

Starting stock and plant sex: Sunrise Solo is a hermaphrodite-type candidate; Honey Gold has separate male and female plants. Confirm the actual stock and sex form. A count of mapped plants alone does not establish how many bear fruit.

Avoid frost and waterlogging. Honey Gold needs male and female plants; Sunrise Solo is hermaphrodite.

Cold-area check: these subtropical references do not establish suitability here. Confirm a frost-protected position before buying.

Buying advice: Planning choice for warm sites: Sunrise Solo. Confirm plant sex/form with the nursery.

Expected picking season: no single local cultivar window established. Reference seasons below are not a forecast.

Reference only — KwaZulu-Natal: Apr–Jan.

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production, PDF pp. 18–19 (regional reference; confirm current nursery stock)](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

Source: [KwaZulu-Natal Department of Agriculture and Rural Development, 'Fruit and Nut Production in KZN' (Horticultural Advisory Notes), section 1.6 Papaya, 'Bearing age', p. 18](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN, Bearing age, p. 18](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Papaya: Bearing age, p. 18](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Papaya: Yields, p. 19](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Papaya: Sex forms, p. 18](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

### Num-num

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: edible ripe berries.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Edible part and local use: The edible berry must be distinguished from bark, which the source describes as containing a poisonous glucoside.

Protect young plants from cold; use well-drained soil in sun or semi-shade. SANBI describes frost tenderness and tolerance of sea breezes.

Buying advice: Ask for botanically identified Carissa bispinosa and local provenance. The checked source supplies no named fruit cultivar.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica, carissa-bispinosa](https://pza.sanbi.org/carissa-bispinosa)

### Karoo num-num

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: ripe num-num fruit — identity must be confirmed.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Edible part and local use: SANBI's botanical account includes C. haematocarpa among South African Carissa. Its identity is bridged to C. bispinosa by the current SANBI assessment; no distinct Karoo cultivar is established.

Current SANBI taxonomic bridge: Listed among synonyms of Carissa bispinosa. This is identity evidence, not a new fruit cultivar or an independent picking window.

Confirm botanical identity before using this catalogue entry as a separate fruit enterprise. Do not count it twice merely because the same plant is also labelled C. bispinosa.

Buying advice: Ask a local botanical nursery to confirm the plant's identity and suitable provenance; no primary named cultivar or exact frost threshold was verified.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica, carissa-sebrabergensis](https://pza.sanbi.org/carissa-sebrabergensis)

### Num-num

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: Ripe fruit, fresh or preserved.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Coastal plant; allow for thorns near children and paths.

Buying advice: Ask for a locally suitable fruiting plant; no named food cultivar is established by this source.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: carissa-macrocarpa](https://pza.sanbi.org/carissa-macrocarpa)

### Sour fig

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: ripe fruit.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Edible part and local use: The source identifies ripe fruit as food. June–October is flowering, not a fruit-picking window.

This sun-loving coastal groundcover can bind sandy soil. SANBI records frost damage, so check cold exposure before using it inland.

Buying advice: Confirm Carpobrotus deliciosus; do not substitute another sour-fig species merely because the common name matches.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica, carpobrotus-deliciosus](https://pza.sanbi.org/carpobrotus-deliciosus)

### Sour fig

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: Ripe fruit.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Full sun and well-drained ground; a waterwise Cape groundcover. Flowering dates are not picking dates.

Buying advice: Use correctly identified local planting material; no named cultivar is sourced.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: carpobrotus-edulis](https://pza.sanbi.org/carpobrotus-edulis)

### Pecan

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: nut in shell.

First crop reference: 5 years. Light cropping at about year 5 in the KZN guide, for irrigated areas with hot summers, cold winters and low growing-season humidity. It identifies dry Zululand/Lowveld river valleys as suitable regional areas. Propagation, cultivar and nursery age are not specified; this is a qualified general reference, not an expected farm quantity. Actual timing depends on variety and site care.

Established production reference: 12–13 years. Full production around years 12–13 in the general KZN guide. Cultivar, propagation, density and management affect actual output; mature ages do not automatically create an annual kg/tree curve.

Pecan guide output — dry nut-in-shell hectare basis: The guide gives conservative 750, average 800–1,200 and good 1,500+ kg/ha Dry-in-Shell. It separately lists alternative tree spacings and later thinning, so one density is not assumed. These are unaged hectare benchmarks; shell weight is not edible kernel weight and no generic kg/tree curve is derived.

Use compatible pollen-shedding and receptive varieties. Wet-summer areas need scab-resistant choices; early nut maturity alone does not establish pollination compatibility.

Buying advice: SAPPA shortlist: wetter KZN/Lowveld — Ukulinga, Cape Fear, Choctaw; wet, colder KZN — Barton; drier Highveld — Barton, Pawnee, Wichita; dry western areas — Wichita, Choctaw, Western Schley. The inferred climate group alone cannot distinguish all these areas. Confirm local humidity, soils and the pollination pair before buying.

Pollination: needs cross pollinator. Check the chosen cultivar's requirements with the nursery.

Regional reference: pecan nuts. South Africa (general — Southern Hemisphere phenology; main areas Vaalharts/Northern Cape, Lower Orange River). Irrigated production reference; confirm cultivar, pollination, summer heat and water capacity. Planning reference when established; confirm local picking dates. No food quantity or first-year crop promised.

Source: [Lötze, E., 'Literature Review: Factors influencing pollination of pecans for commercial production', published by SAPPA](https://www.sappa.za.org/download/16968/?tmstv=1790592292)

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN, Pecan yield; printed p.22, p. 26](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

### Pennywort

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: cooked leaves.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Confirmed South African vegetable use: The author identifies C. asiatica as a cooked South African vegetable. Centella species can be difficult to distinguish; nearby C. coriacea food or yield evidence is not transferred. No food picking months, first harvest duration or kg/plant is provided.

Confirm exact identity and record the cooked-leaf product; medicinal use does not establish a food production forecast.

Buying advice: Obtain identified Centella asiatica material from a reputable nursery; no regional food cultivar or measured annual leaf yield is verified.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [Long, H.S. (2014), University of Johannesburg MSc Botany thesis abstract](https://ujcontent.uj.ac.za/esploro/outputs/graduate/The-ethnobotany-and-pharmacognosy-of-selected/9912838407691)

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: pods.

foodForest.title: Avocado
lines: 1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: fruit.

First crop reference: 2–3 years. Bruyns Hill, Natal Midlands bioclimatic group 2; irrigated Hass on clonal Duke 7 rootstock, 7 x 7 m (200 trees/ha), planted 1982–1984. The paper reports Hass starting in its second season and Fuerte in its third. The two-to-three-year reference describes those trial cultivars, not every avocado or nursery starting age. Actual timing depends on variety and site care.

Established production reference: 6–8 years. In this irrigated, intensively managed Natal Midlands trial, Hass reached about 20 t/ha at age 6 and orchards approached maximum sustainable average yield by age 8. This is a trial-specific bearing reference; there is no national plateau or automatically interpolated age-yield curve.

Production reference: 100–112.5 kg/plant. Same-trial arithmetic at the initial 200 trees/ha: 20,000 kg/ha / 200 = 100 kg/tree at age 6; sustainable average 22,500 kg/ha / 200 = 112.5 kg/tree. At age 3, 10,000 kg/ha / 200 = 50 kg/tree equivalent. These are average-equivalent reference values for the named Hass/Duke 7 orchard conditions, not measured individual-tree yields or default production for a different density, cultivar, climate or management. Intermediate ages are not inferred.

Hass age benchmarks — irrigated Natal Midlands trial: Hass on Duke 7, initially 200 trees/ha at Bruyns Hill (Natal Midlands bioclimatic group 2), with intensive irrigation and nutrition. Age 3: 10,000 kg/ha; age 6: 20,000 kg/ha; sustainable average about 22,500 kg/ha. Same-study density permits equivalents of 50 kg/tree at age 3 and 100 kg/tree at age 6; there is no reference for every intermediate age. These orchard benchmarks are conditional on good resources, comparable climate and timely orchard management, including Phytophthora control and thinning; do not auto-fill farm quantities.
Keep roots well drained; water matters during flowering.

foodForest.title: Spiny monkey orange
lines: 1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: Ripe fruit pulp only.

First crop reference: 3–5 years. The review attributes this 3–5-year age to Avakoudjo et al.'s study in Benin, West Africa, rather than a South African bearing trial. Propagation method and local conditions must be confirmed before using it at a South African site; it is not a locally validated age or a yield-by-age curve. Actual timing depends on variety and site care.

Production reference: 40–100 kg/plant. The review reports 40–100 kg per tree stand without an annual period, mature age, matched cultivar or South African field conditions. Retain the original per-plant weight as context only: do not relabel it kg/year, spread it across months or treat it as a farm forecast.

Harvest interval with unverified South African geography: The review states August–December but does not identify a locality for that interval. Related monkey-orange literature discusses this interval in Zimbabwe and more than one Strychnos species; it does not establish a South African spinosa picking calendar. The former South Africa (general) window is withheld. Record the farm's own ripe-pulp months; seeds and unripe pulp are not ordinary food.

Geography of the review's bearing-age citation: The 2021 review cites this Benin study for its 3–5-year bearing-age statement. The cited source's geography is West Africa, not a South African orchard. Retain the review's numeric statement with this condition; no local annual yield curve is supplied.
Seeds and unripe fruit are toxic. Keep children away from unsupervised harvesting and preparation.
Buying advice: Confirm identity and appropriate handling before including it in a food plan; no named cultivar is sourced.
Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

cases.markdown:
## Production purchases and variety assumptions

Research checked 11 October 2026. Buy only proposed stock after checking local suitability. Existing plants and structures are inventory, not repeat purchases. Early/middle/late describes picking order; compatible flowering is a separate pollination check. Expected seasons describe established production, not guaranteed food this year.

### Feijoa

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: fruit.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Cultivar-dependent pollen compatibility: Primary Brazilian germplasm experiment found both compatibility classes. Biological evidence supports checking the actual cultivar and compatible pollen, not assigning one universal species category or copying its calendar to South Africa.

South African research context: Government confirms ARC evaluated feijoa; no trial result, cultivar, harvest month or yield follows from this mention.

Check the actual cultivar's pollen needs. A primary trial includes self-compatible and self-incompatible plants.

Record local ripe picking dates and output. Foreign cultivar seasons do not establish a South African season.

Buying advice: Ask the nursery to name the cultivar or identify a seedling and provide local fruiting and compatible-pollen evidence. 'Fruit Salad Tree' is a common sales label and does not identify a tested cultivar.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [dos Santos et al. (2007), Evidence of late-acting self-incompatibility in Acca sellowiana, Revista Brasileira de Fruticultura 29(1)](https://new.scielo.br/j/rbf/a/3Wh7WGGbVFkHckM7R5GDJLc/?ilang=pt_BR&lang=pt)

Source: [South African Yearbook 2003/04, ARC tropical/subtropical crop research](https://www.gcis.gov.za/sites/default/files/docs/resourcecentre/yearbook/2004/18scitec.pdf)

### Quiver tree

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: young flower buds.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Young flower-bud food use: The edible product is the young flower bud. June–July flowering does not establish the exact pre-opening picking dates, first bud-bearing age or edible kg/plant.

Match cultivation to this arid-land tree and well-drained conditions.

Record young-bud picking separately from flowering or ornamental growth.

Buying advice: Obtain correctly identified legal nursery stock and local growing advice. No food-yield cultivar or maturity curve is verified.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Aloidendron dichotomum](https://pza.sanbi.org/aloidendron-dichotomum)

### Pineapple

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: Pineapple fruit; whole fruit and processed portions have different weights.

First crop reference: 18 months. Hluhluwe production-cycle reference: 18 months / 12 = 1.5 years. The source explicitly says cycle length varies greatly. Starting material, cultivar, weather and flower initiation matter; this is neither a universal first-harvest date nor a 12-month annual yield. Actual timing depends on variety and site care.

Hluhluwe crop-cycle output: Regional hectare reference: conservative 50 t/ha, average 60–75 t/ha, good 80 t/ha per production crop. The same page describes a normal 18-month Hluhluwe cycle. These are not kg/plant/year or a forecast for a household planting.

Cultivar and renewal choice: Queen and Smooth Cayenne serve different uses. The guide's example fruit weights (Queen 0.75 kg; Smooth Cayenne 2 kg) are cultivar descriptions, not annual yields per plant. Queen is re-established after the plant crop in this system.

Climate and calendar conditions: Frost sensitivity and drainage constrain the site. Year-round planting at Hluhluwe is a planting reference, not an all-year household picking window; cooler sites use warmer planting months.

Use a warm, frost-free, well-drained site. The KZN production reference is Hluhluwe; it does not establish suitability throughout South Africa.

Record planting and actual picking dates. Year-round commercial planting or marketing does not mean every planted pineapple gives fruit in every month.

Buying advice: KZN guide: Queen is a fresh-fruit candidate; Smooth Cayenne is mainly a processing candidate. Confirm clean crowns/suckers, local suitability and crop-cycle advice with a nursery. Queen re-establishment after the plant crop belongs in the future plan.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple: Bearing Age, p. 22](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple, p. 22](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple: Spacing and Cultivars, p. 22](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

Source: [KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple: Climate and Planting Times, p. 22](https://www.kzndard.gov.za/images/Documents/Horticulture/Veg_prod/Fruit%20and%20%20Nut%20Production%20in%20KZN.pdf)

### Waterblommetjie

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: flowers and flower buds.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Waterblommetjie food product and establishment: Western Cape pond food; vigorous winter/spring flowering and winter shop availability are qualitative seasonal evidence, not a numeric picking calendar. Seedlings reach flowering size in one season under ideal conditions, not a universal age-in-years guarantee.

Ideal seedling establishment: Qualitative ideal-condition establishment duration; it is not inserted into a generic tree-age curve.

Start tubers in loam in shallow pond water; move deeper into sun after strong growth.

Record edible flowers/buds and pond area. Dormant tubers resume growth as autumn water returns in the winter-rainfall cycle.

Buying advice: Obtain correctly identified pond plants. Confirm local pond conditions and actual picking dates; no pond-area yield or planting density is sourced.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Aponogeton distachyos](https://pza.sanbi.org/aponogeton-distachyos)

### Rooibos

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: young shoots for dried rooibos tea.

First crop reference: 12–18 months. First commercial cutting readiness at 12–18 months in the described Cape production system. The account discusses sowing and transfer to plantations but does not explicitly define whether the clock starts at sowing or planting out. Confirm starting stock and timing locally. This is tea-shoot establishment, not fruit-tree bearing. Actual timing depends on variety and site care.

Commercial tea cutting cycle and product: Selected commercial rooibos forms in the Cederberg winter-rainfall region are cut annually December–April, retaining older branches. Cut shoots are chopped, bruised, oxidised and dried. Fresh shoot kg and dried tea kg are separate products. The account describes replacement after up to five harvest years, not a mature kg/plant curve.

Match planting to acidic, sandy winter-rainfall soils and locally suitable rooibos forms.

Keep fresh-cut shoot weights separate from processed dried tea; record the actual processing output.

Buying advice: Ask a local rooibos nursery or adviser for correctly identified, locally proven planting material. The Cape cycle is not a nationwide tea forecast.

Expected picking season: no single local cultivar window established. Reference seasons below are not a forecast.

Reference only — Cederberg / Western Cape winter-rainfall commercial rooibos: Dec–Apr.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Aspalathus linearis](https://pza.sanbi.org/aspalathus-linearis)

### Creeping foxglove

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: leaves for cooked greens.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Documented leaf food use: The article explicitly identifies the catalogue subspecies and edible leaves. Spring/summer flowering is not a leaf-picking calendar.

Use a moist growing position, with semi-shade or sun where water is adequate.

Control rooted runners so this fast groundcover does not smother neighbouring plants.

Buying advice: Buy correctly identified subspecies material. Record actual leaf-cutting dates and weights; no local yield variety or first-cutting duration is verified.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Asystasia gangetica subsp. micrantha](https://pza.sanbi.org/asystasia-gangetica)

### Powder-puff tree

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: young leaves reported edible — specialist review needed.

Food-use review: confirm identity, edible part and appropriate preparation with a qualified local adviser before including this plant as household food. Held out of ordinary food totals and picking jobs.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Edible-part and safety review: The same source reports poison in seeds, bark, wood and roots. Guava-like fruit appearance is not evidence of edible fruit.

Poisonous parts must remain visible: The account records fish-stunning use. No such use is recommended, and no household fruit food claim is made.

Keep this tree in mapped inventory and do not count it as household food until identity and a safe edible-leaf preparation are reviewed.

SANBI describes humid coastal/estuarine conditions and no tolerance of even mild frost.

Buying advice: Ask a specialist nursery about lawful provenance and local site fit. Resolve the food-use question before purchasing it as a household crop.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica, barringtonia-racemosa](https://pza.sanbi.org/barringtonia-racemosa)

### Malabar spinach

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: leaves and tender stems.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Leaf vegetable identity and warm-climate culture: Florida extension confirms Malabar spinach as a warm-climate leaf vegetable. Its Florida planting and harvest calendar is not a South African calendar.

Cultivation context: Foreign extension reference for support, seed/cutting propagation and warm, moist conditions; no Florida months are imported into the South African plan.

Optimal from-seed cutting-cycle reference — Florida extension: The extension guide reports maturity around 70 days from seed under optimal conditions, followed by hand trimming leaves and young stems. This foreign optimal-condition duration is supplementary; no South African planting date, exact month window or generic tree-age value is inferred.

Provide climbing support and adequate moisture in a warm growing position.

Record successive leaf harvests by planting batch rather than using tree-age production.

Buying advice: Obtain labelled Basella alba material. A South African regional cultivar, kg/plant benchmark and dated picking window remain unverified.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [UF/IFAS Gardening Solutions: Tropical Spinaches](https://gardeningsolutions.ifas.ufl.edu/plants/edibles/vegetables/tropical-spinaches/)

Source: [UF/IFAS: Cultivation of Malabar Spinach in Florida](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/HS1371)

Source: [UF/IFAS: Florida Cultivation Guide for Malabar Spinach, Harvest and Storage](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/HS1371)

### Brown ivory

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: ripe fruit.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Edible part and local use: January–July is fruit appearance in SANBI's account, not an explicit ripe-picking interval.

Fruit-development duration has context: This is flower-to-fruit development, not years from planting. Its South African January–July fruiting statement is not an observed household picking window.

Use frost-free conditions: SANBI describes frost sensitivity despite drought resistance, with natural low-altitude riverbank bushveld in northern KwaZulu-Natal, Mpumalanga and Limpopo.

Buying advice: Ask for Berchemia discolor, not red ivory (B. zeyheri). Record actual local ripe-picking months.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica, berchemia-discolor](https://pza.sanbi.org/berchemia-discolor)

Source: [World Agroforestry, Agroforestree Database, Berchemia discolor, p. 1](https://apps.worldagroforestry.org/treedb/AFTPDFS/Berchemia_discolor.pdf)

### Shepherd's tree

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: fruit; traditionally prepared flower buds.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Edible part and local use: SANBI also records flower-bud pickle use. Root porridge/coffee references are not instructions to harvest roots or a complete preparation guide.

This hardy, drought-resistant tree occurs in drier southern African regions.

SANBI reports that leaf browsing can taint cattle milk. No feed ration is recommended.

Buying advice: Ask for correctly identified, lawfully sourced stock and check current protected-tree collection requirements before harvesting existing wild trees.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica, boscia-albitrunca](https://pza.sanbi.org/boscia-albitrunca)

### Pigeon pea

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: dry grain or green immature seed; fodder is a separate product.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

SA cultivar maturity and grain trial: Malekutu, Mpumalanga, 1998/99; rainfed mid-December sowing, sandy loam, no fertiliser. Paired days after planting / grain kg/ha: ICPL 88039 127 / 1823; ICPL 85010 129 / 1525; ICPL 87091 140 / 1299; ICPL 87051 193 / 978; ICEAP 00053 231 / 918. Grain differences within each trial were not significant. Visually checked Tables 1–2 (PDF pp43–44). These are dry-grain observations, not green-seed picking dates or nationwide yield defaults.

Tentative newer ARC planting comparison: Potchefstroom 2020/21, good rainfall season: ICEAP01258 versus ICEAP01284 and 22 October versus 25 November sowing. Currant fruit food use and phenology: The primary account establishes edible ripe fruit and October–June fruit appearance. That interval includes developing fruit and is retained only as phenology, not a ripe picking calendar. No annual food kg or bearing age is supplied.

Pick ripe fruit and record drying separately.

This shrub suits exposed coastal gardens and dune stabilisation; confirm local provenance.

Buying advice: Ask an indigenous nursery for exact species and local material. No regional high-yield food cultivar is verified.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Searsia lucida](https://pza.sanbi.org/searsia-lucida)

### Natal currant

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: ripe fruit.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Edible Natal currant fruit and local phenology: The primary account establishes edible ripe fruit and February–July fruit appearance. That interval includes developing fruit and is retained only as phenology, not a ripe picking calendar. No annual food kg or bearing age is supplied.

Allow fruit to ripen. This drought-resistant shrub can form a hedge; prune to suit the space.

Buying advice: Confirm the exact species with a local indigenous-plant nursery; no tested regional cultivar or quantified yield selection is established.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Searsia natalensis](https://pza.sanbi.org/searsia-natalensis)

### Kuni bush

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: ripe dried fruit.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Named traditional dried-fruit food use: The discussion explicitly includes S. undulata among edible dried ripe currant fruits and traditional fermentation uses. Its host article species calendar is not transferred to S. undulata.

Exact species and habitat: Assessment identifies the catalogue species and Northern/Western Cape distribution; it does not provide a harvest calendar or food yield.

Record ripe fruit picking and drying separately. No storage duration or fermentation recipe is assigned.

Buying advice: Confirm the exact species and local provenance; the SANBI assessment places it on stony fynbos/karroid slopes of the Northern and Western Cape.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Searsia burchellii, food-use discussion naming S. undulata](https://pza.sanbi.org/searsia-burchellii)

Source: [SANBI Red List: Searsia undulata](https://redlist.sanbi.org/species.php?species=5522-153)

### White milkwood

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: ripe berries.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Edible part and local use: SANBI qualifies the food statement; it is about ripe berries, not latex, bark or roots. Fruit presence February–September does not establish ripe picking throughout.

Species identification in KwaZulu-Natal: The primary study records confusion with Bridelia micrantha. It does not supply a safe harvest calendar or kg/tree.

Shelter this coastal tree from direct salt-laden sea wind; SANBI reports salt burn despite its coastal habitat.

Buying advice: Ask a nursery to confirm the species and lawful provenance. Check current collection requirements before taking plants or products from existing trees.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica, sideroxylon-inerme](https://pza.sanbi.org/sideroxylon-inerme)

Source: [University of KwaZulu-Natal, Phytochemical and elemental studies of two indigenous medicinal plants](https://researchspace.ukzn.ac.za/server/api/core/bitstreams/ee2eb137-9aa4-43b9-ae69-392311b96970/content)

### Spiny monkey orange

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: Ripe fruit pulp only.

First crop reference: 3–5 years. The review attributes this 3–5-year age to Avakoudjo et al.'s study in Benin, West Africa, rather than a South African bearing trial. Propagation method and local conditions must be confirmed before using it at a South African site; it is not a locally validated age or a yield-by-age curve. Actual timing depends on variety and site care.

Production reference: 40–100 kg/plant. The review reports 40–100 kg per tree stand without an annual period, mature age, matched cultivar or South African field conditions. Retain the original per-plant weight as context only: do not relabel it kg/year, spread it across months or treat it as a farm forecast.

Harvest interval with unverified South African geography: The review states August–December but does not identify a locality for that interval. Related monkey-orange literature discusses this interval in Zimbabwe and more than one Strychnos species; it does not establish a South African spinosa picking calendar. The former South Africa (general) window is withheld. Record the farm's own ripe-pulp months; seeds and unripe pulp are not ordinary food.

Geography of the review's bearing-age citation: The 2021 review cites this Benin study for its 3–5-year bearing-age statement. The cited source's geography is West Africa, not a South African orchard. Retain the review's numeric statement with this condition; no local annual yield curve is supplied.

Seeds and unripe fruit are toxic. Keep children away from unsupervised harvesting and preparation.

Buying advice: Confirm identity and appropriate handling before including it in a food plan; no named cultivar is sourced.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [FAO Ecocrop / ICRAF: Strychnos spinosa](https://ecocrop.apps.fao.org/ecocrop/srv/en/cropView?id=10135)

Source: [Undervalued Spiny Monkey Orange (Strychnos spinosa Lam.): An Indigenous Fruit for Sustainable Food-Nutrition and Economic Prosperity (peer-reviewed review, PMC8703348)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703348/)

Source: [Omotayo & Aremu (2021), Undervalued Spiny Monkey Orange, section 3](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703348/)

Source: [Avakoudjo et al. (2020), Local Knowledge, Uses, and Factors Determining the Use of Strychnos spinosa Organs in Benin (West Africa), abstract](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12231-019-09481-0)

### Waterberry

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: Ripe berries.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Flowering and fruit appearance, not a ripe picking calendar: The original PROTA account dates flowering and fruiting but does not date ripening. SANBI describes red to dark-purple ripe berries without ripe picking months. The November–March observation is retained as southern African phenology; local food-ready picking months remain unknown.

Water-loving: a dry site needs a dependable moisture source. Flowering for bees is not a honey-harvest forecast.

Buying advice: Choose a moist position and local provenance; no named cultivar is sourced.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: syzygium-cordatum](https://pza.sanbi.org/syzygium-cordatum)

Source: [Brink, M. (2008), PROTA4U: Syzygium cordatum, Growth and development](https://prota.prota4u.org/protav8.asp?p=Syzygium+cordatum)

### Dune spinach

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: young leafy tops and stems.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Leaf vegetable harvesting and preparation: New rainy-season growth gives the best tops; wash off coastal sand thoroughly and boil for the documented vegetable preparation. August–November flowering is not leaf availability.

Harvest young leafy tops; wash off sand before cooking.

Use well-drained coastal sand and keep divided plants moist until established.

Buying advice: Obtain correctly identified coastal planting material; record local growth and leaf-picking months because rainy seasons differ across South Africa.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Tetragonia decumbens](https://pza.sanbi.org/tetragonia-decumbens)

### Kinkelbossie

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: young shoots, cooked.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Young-shoot vegetable use: The account describes boiling young shoots until tender. September–January flowering is not a shoot harvest calendar; fodder output is not household food kg.

Harvest young shoots for cooking. Record food harvest separately from animal fodder.

Use a sunny, well-drained coastal, fynbos or Karoo position suited to this water-wise pioneer.

Buying advice: Obtain correctly identified local planting material; no named food cultivar or annual kg/plant benchmark is sourced.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Tetragonia fruticosa](https://pza.sanbi.org/tetragonia-fruticosa)

### Veldkool

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: flower buds.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Edible bud identity: Coastal-sand perennial with edible congested flower buds. The stated July–September flowering interval does not identify exact unopened-bud picking months.

Record picking of young flower buds separately from open flowers.

Match the plant to well-drained coastal sandy conditions and its seasonal growth.

Buying advice: Use exact-species nursery identification; no first bud harvest age or food kg/plant benchmark is verified.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Trachyandra ciliata](https://pza.sanbi.org/trachyandra-ciliata)

### Pigeonwood

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: young leaves for cooked greens.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Documented young-leaf food use: The human food product is young leaves. Berries described as bird/bat food are not promoted to a human fruit harvest. No leaf cutting age, exact months or household leaf kg is given.

Match this fast pioneer to warm, moist eastern/northern conditions; protect damp, shaded seedlings.

Record young-leaf harvest separately from fruit consumed by wildlife.

Buying advice: Use correctly identified local planting material; no named leaf-food cultivar or quantified annual food output is verified.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: Trema orientalis](https://pza.sanbi.org/trema-orientalis)

### Wild garlic

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: leaves and edible flowers.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Edible part and local use: Leaves and flowers are documented culinary parts. Medicinal bulb use does not make every part a food.

It tolerates prolonged drought but grows better with regular water. SANBI records its eastern South African distribution.

Buying advice: Ask for Tulbaghia violacea, rather than a plant identified only as wild garlic. Record local leaf and flower picking separately.

Expected picking season: no single local cultivar window established. Reference seasons below are not a forecast.

Reference only — Eastern South African botanical account — edible flowers only: Jan–Apr.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica, tulbaghia-violacea](https://pza.sanbi.org/tulbaghia-violacea)

### Blueberry

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: fruit.

First crop reference: 2–3 years. The USDA FAS industry reference concerns fruit of export quality after up to two to three years. Earlier light fruiting is not excluded; this is not a guaranteed first harvest date. Actual timing depends on variety and site care.

Established production reference: 6–7 years. KZN advice describes Vaccinium species and lists rabbiteye cultivars Tifblue, Beckyblue and Climax. This reference is not specific to southern highbush blueberries.

Check soil acidity, cultivar chilling, irrigation and pollination requirements before buying.

Buying advice: Warm-climate candidate: Biloxi, a low-chill southern highbush cultivar, reported by a nursery producing stock in South Africa. Obtain a compatible southern highbush pollination partner. Early flowering can suffer spring frost; local soil, chill and harvest dates still need checking. Do not substitute rabbiteye plants as a highbush cultivar.

Pollination: partly self fertile. Check the chosen cultivar's requirements with the nursery.

Expected picking season: no single local cultivar window established. Reference seasons below are not a forecast.

Reference only — Western Cape (Hex River and Wolseley trial sites): Aug–Nov.

Reference only — South Africa (national, USDA FAS GAIN): Sep–Feb.

### Wild medlar

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: Ripe fruit, fresh or dried.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Wider fruiting observations, not a ripe picking interval: This account separately distinguishes green unripe and brown ripe fruit, but its November–April biology sentence does not date that ripening change. The wider interval remains southern African phenology. SANBI's January–April description of ripe edible fruit supplies the food-ready regional reference.

Confirm local establishment conditions before relying on the regional fruiting reference.

Buying advice: Request locally appropriate fruiting stock; no named cultivar is sourced.

Expected picking season: no single local cultivar window established. Reference seasons below are not a forecast.

Reference only — South Africa (general; SA distribution given as Eastern Cape, Free State, Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal, Limpopo, Mpumalanga, North West, Northern Cape): Jan–Apr.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica: vangueria-infausta](https://pza.sanbi.org/vangueria-infausta)

Source: [Vangueria infausta | PlantZAfrica (SANBI)](https://pza.sanbi.org/vangueria-infausta)

### Grape vine

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: fruit.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Flame Seedless year 4 — Hex River Valley enterprise budget: Year 4 commercial budget: 4,400 cartons/ha at 4.5 kg/carton = 19,800 kg/ha. The source does not provide matched vines/ha or row/vine spacing, so no kg/vine is derived. This is a budget assumption for one cultivar and region, not a generic full-bearing age or a local mapped-vine production record.

Match the vineyard variety to its production region, water and support system. The national supply season combines several regions.

Buying advice: DAFF industry reference: earlier Prime Seedless, Sugraone and Flame Seedless; later Dauphine and Crimson Seedless. SATI identifies Orange River choices including Prime, Thompson Seedless and Sugraone. Confirm local dates and stock; the industry sequence is not a KZN farm calendar.

Pollination: self fertile. Check the chosen cultivar's requirements with the nursery.

Expected picking season: no single local cultivar window established. Reference seasons below are not a forecast.

Reference only — South Africa — Northern Province(s) region (SATI production region; mild sub-tropical, earliest SA harvest): Nov–Dec.

Reference only — South Africa (overall, all regions combined): Nov–May.

Source: [DAFF, Table grape market value chain profile (2012), p. 1](https://www.nda.gov.za/phocadownloadpap/Agricultural_Marketing_Commodity_Profiles/Table%20grape%20market%20value%20chain%20profile%202012.pdf)

### Ginger

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: fresh rhizomes; dried ginger recorded separately.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

South African trial harvest duration and native yields: Pretoria Hillcrest rain-shelter trial, 2015/16 and 2016/17, drip irrigation on sandy clay loam. Commercial ginger Z. officinale at eight months: 38.3 t/ha fresh and 8.8 t/ha dry rhizomes in the well-watered treatment; African ginger was a different species with different values. No matched plant density is supplied, so no kg/plant or household drying conversion is derived. The abstract says open field, while Methods specifies rain shelter; conditions are retained.

Confirmed culinary species and product: Extension identifies culinary ginger rhizomes used as spice, preserves and beverages. Florida planting and harvest months are not imported into the South African calendar.

Harvest recommendation: The author abstract recommends harvest seven to eight months after planting; it is a rhizome crop-cycle duration, not a full-bearing tree age.

Use the planting date to record the rhizome harvest cycle. The Pretoria trial reference is conditional, not a fixed calendar across climates.

Record fresh rhizome and dried spice weights separately; keep edible ginger distinct from ornamental or African ginger species.

Buying advice: Ask a local supplier for healthy, identified Zingiber officinale planting rhizomes; no South African cultivar-specific yield curve is verified.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [Gatabazi et al. (2022), Scientia Horticulturae 304:111353, p. 17](https://repository.up.ac.za/bitstream/handle/2263/91386/Gatabazi_Effect_2022.pdf?sequence=1)

Source: [UF/IFAS: Ginger, Galangal, and Turmeric Production in Florida](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/EP638)

Source: [University of Pretoria author manuscript: Gatabazi et al. (2022)](https://repository.up.ac.za/items/00edc5cf-b651-48d9-832f-f0b8b1d53c33)

### Buffalo thorn

1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: ripe berries.

Time to first crop: not sourced; do not rely on newly planted stock for immediate food.

Edible part and local use: SANBI describes dry, slightly sweet ripe pulp. Fruit remaining on leafless trees March–August is persistence, not a verified six-month picking season.

SANBI records a wide range from frost-free coast to winter-frost regions. Its hooked and straight thorns matter when choosing access routes.

Buying advice: Ask for an identified buffalo-thorn plant suited to local conditions; the checked source supplies no named food cultivar.

Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

Source: [SANBI PlantZAfrica, ziziphus-mucronata](https://pza.sanbi.org/ziziphus-mucronata)

## Production purchases and variety assumptions

Research checked 11 October 2026. Buy only proposed stock after checking local suitability. Existing plants and structures are inventory, not repeat purchases. Early/middle/late describes picking order; compatible flowering is a separate pollination check. Expected seasons describe established production, not guaranteed food this year.

foodForest.title: Banana
lines: 0 existing; 3 proposed. Products: fruit (bunch of bananas).
Count assumption: 1 banana circle(s) × 3 planted bananas. Followers are not additional planted trees.

First crop reference: 13–20 months. KZN DARD explicitly states the planting-to-harvest and harvest-to-harvest range. Converted months to years (13/12 to 20/12). This is not a dated forecast or an annual all-month harvest window. Actual timing depends on variety and site care.

Annual plantation output: KZN plantation reference per year: conservative 20–25 t/ha, average 25–30 t/ha, good 40+ t/ha. This is annual area production; it is not the weight of one bunch or a measured age-yield curve for three plants in a banana circle.

Cultivar, planting and crop cycle: The KZN guide gives 13–20 months for both the first planting-to-harvest cycle and subsequent harvest-to-harvest cycles. It lists different commercial densities for Williams, Grand Nain and Chinese Cavendish. A banana circle counts as three planted bananas here; replacement followers are stages of those mats, not extra mapped trees or guaranteed year-round supply.
Warm, frost-free conditions and dependable water are needed. Keep a replacement follower after the fruiting stem is removed.
Assumed planting variety: Grand Nain for a warm site; use the wind/cold alternatives in the buying advice if those conditions apply. Local picking months remain unconfirmed.
Buying advice: Cooler KZN: Williams; warmer valleys: Grand Nain; windy coast: Chinese Cavendish. Buy clean planting material. These are climate choices, not early/middle/late seasons.
Edible bananas set fruit without pollination.
Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.
